  <h2 class="dash-section-title">The toolkit</h2>

  <div class="dash-cards about-tools">

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">
      <div class="dash-xcard-top">
        <span class="dash-xnum tile-purple">sf</span>
        <span class="dash-xchip">Vector</span>
      </div>
      <h3>Simple Features</h3>
      <p>Reading GeoJSON and shapefiles, assigning and transforming coordinate
      systems, buffering, spatial joins and point-in-polygon counting.</p>
      <div class="dash-xmeta"><span>Used in <b>all five</b> exercises</span></div>
    </div>

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">
      <div class="dash-xcard-top">
        <span class="dash-xnum tile-blue">tm</span>
        <span class="dash-xchip chip-blue">Cartography</span>
      </div>
      <h3>tmap 4.x</h3>
      <p>Choropleths, classification methods, colour schemes, small multiples,
      raster layers and interactive maps, written against the v4 API.</p>
      <div class="dash-xmeta"><span>Used in <b>four</b> exercises</span></div>
    </div>

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">
      <div class="dash-xcard-top">
        <span class="dash-xnum tile-coral">sp</span>
        <span class="dash-xchip chip-coral">Point patterns</span>
      </div>
      <h3>spatstat</h3>
      <p>Kernel density estimation, bandwidth selection, the Clark-Evans test and
      the G, F, K and L summary functions with Monte Carlo envelopes.</p>
      <div class="dash-xmeta"><span>Used in <b>two</b> exercises</span></div>
    </div>

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">
      <div class="dash-xcard-top">
        <span class="dash-xnum tile-green">tr</span>
        <span class="dash-xchip chip-green">Raster</span>
      </div>
      <h3>terra</h3>
      <p>The raster data model: building grids, rasterising point layers, and
      converting density surfaces for cartographic output.</p>
      <div class="dash-xmeta"><span>Used in <b>two</b> exercises</span></div>
    </div>

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">
      <div class="dash-xcard-top">
        <span class="dash-xnum tile-amber">gg</span>
        <span class="dash-xchip chip-amber">Statistics</span>
      </div>
      <h3>ggstatsplot</h3>
      <p>Charts that carry their own confirmatory test, turning a visual impression
      into a reportable correlation with a confidence interval.</p>
      <div class="dash-xmeta"><span>Used in <b>one</b> exercise</span></div>
    </div>

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">
      <div class="dash-xcard-top">
        <span class="dash-xnum tile-purple">tv</span>
        <span class="dash-xchip">Wrangling</span>
      </div>
      <h3>tidyverse</h3>
      <p>Import, reshape and join with <b>readr</b>, <b>dplyr</b>, <b>tidyr</b>,
      <b>ggplot2</b> and <b>purrr</b> throughout.</p>
      <div class="dash-xmeta"><span>Used in <b>all five</b> exercises</span></div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <h2 class="dash-section-title">Course progress</h2>

  <div class="about-timeline">

    <div class="about-tl-item done">
      <div class="about-tl-dot tile-purple"></div>
      <div class="about-tl-body">
        <div class="about-tl-head">
          <h3>Lesson 1 · Geospatial data models and mapping</h3>
          <span class="dash-xchip">3 exercises</span>
        </div>
        <p>Vector and raster data models, geographic versus projected coordinate
        systems, and thematic mapping principles. Produced the first choropleths of
        Singapore's planning subzones, then went beyond the built-in classification
        methods to percentile and box maps whose breaks come from the data
        distribution itself.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="about-tl-item done">
      <div class="about-tl-dot tile-coral"></div>
      <div class="about-tl-body">
        <div class="about-tl-head">
          <h3>Lesson 2 · Spatial point patterns analysis</h3>
          <span class="dash-xchip chip-blue">2 exercises</span>
        </div>
        <p>First-order methods describing where events are dense, and second-order
        methods describing whether events attract or repel one another and at what
        distance. The headline result: Singapore's 1,925 childcare centres are
        strongly clustered, <b>R = 0.552</b>, and the pattern survives every test
        applied to it.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="about-tl-item current">
      <div class="about-tl-dot tile-amber"></div>
      <div class="about-tl-body">
        <div class="about-tl-head">
          <h3>Lesson 3 · Spatio-temporal point patterns</h3>
          <span class="dash-xchip chip-amber">In progress</span>
        </div>
        <p>Adding time to the point pattern: spatio-temporal kernel density
        estimation and space-time K-functions, applied to forest fire detections in
        Kepulauan Bangka Belitung, Indonesia.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="about-tl-item todo">
      <div class="about-tl-dot tile-grey"></div>
      <div class="about-tl-body">
        <div class="about-tl-head">
          <h3>Lessons 4 – 10</h3>
          <span class="dash-xchip chip-grey">Ahead</span>
        </div>
        <p>Spatial weights and autocorrelation, emerging hot spot analysis, spatially
        constrained clustering, geographically weighted models, and spatial
        interaction and accessibility modelling.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <h2 class="dash-section-title">How this site is built</h2>

  <div class="dash-cards">

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">

    </div>

    <div class="dash-xcard dash-xcard-empty">

      <h3>R 4.5.2</h3>
      <p>All analysis runs locally and is frozen with <code>freeze: auto</code>, so a
      published result is reproducible from the exact code beside it.</p>
